title: v3.6.0 recommends re-applying the AWS-vended CRDs before the controller (Gateway API stays at v1.6.0)

detection.reason: reads the installed CRD's top-level spec field names (crdSpecFields[], agent 0.4.154+); TargetGroupBinding registerTargetsWithPodAvailabilityZone is v3.6.0's addition — an older agent writes no field list, which reads not projected, never clean

quote: There is no Gateway API graduation in this release -- the controller remains built against Gateway API CRDs v1.6.0 (unchanged from v3.5.0). As a safety measure, we recommend applying the latest AWS-vended CRDs before upgrading the controller.
remediation: Run kubectl apply -k "github.com/aws/eks-charts/stable/aws-load-balancer-controller/crds?ref=master" and config/crd/gateway/gateway-crds.yaml before upgrading when installed with helm. Patch releases 3.6.1 / 3.6.2 need no CRD change.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd targetgroupbindings.elbv2.k8s.aws -o json | jq -r '[.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] as $v | (.spec.versions[] | select(.storage) | .schema.openAPIV3Schema.properties.spec.properties // {} | keys) as $k | "served=\($v | join(",")) spec fields=\($k | join(","))"'  # the installed CRD schema; the 3.6 fields (cross-account AZ registration) absent from the field list means the CRDs were not re-applied for this release

title: v3.6.2's base image distrusts five certificate authorities — OIDC / IdP endpoints signed by them fail from the controller

detection.reason: the controller's only outbound TLS is to the AWS APIs (it never contacts an OIDC issuer — the ALB does); whether those calls go through a TLS-intercepting proxy or a custom --aws-api-endpoints is not a projected fact. The hint names the controller Deployment and the command prints its args and proxy env names

quote: **Controller image rebuilt on a base image that distrusts 5 certificate authorities** The controller image is now built on `eks-distro-minimal-base-nonroot:2026-10-23-1792785692.2023` (from `2026-07-27-1785178906.2023`), which removes 5 distrusted eMudhra/emSign roots from the image CA bundle. Three were present and trusted in the previous base image -- `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, `emSign ECC Root CA - C3` and `emSign Root CA - C1` -- taking the trusted root count from 143 to 140. This affects outbound TLS trust decisions made by the controller; there is no change to controller behavior or configuration. Upstream change: aws/eks-distro-build-tooling#2169. (#4937, @shraddhabang)
remediation: Only when the controller reaches the AWS APIs through a TLS-intercepting proxy (HTTPS_PROXY) or custom --aws-api-endpoints whose certificate chains to one of the five distrusted CAs: TLS verification fails after 3.6.2 and every AWS call errors. Re-issue that certificate from a trusted CA or mount a custom CA bundle (SSL_CERT_FILE). OIDC Ingresses are unaffected — the ALB, not the controller, talks to the issuer.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("aws-load-balancer-controller")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) \(.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image) args=\(.spec.template.spec.containers[0].args // [] | join(" "))"'  # the controller Deployment, its image tag and every flag it runs with; kubectl get deploy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.template.spec.containers[]?.image? // "" | test("aws-load-balancer-controller")) | [.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[]? | select(.name | test("PROXY|SSL_CERT|AWS_CA_BUNDLE")) | .name] | join(",")'  # a proxy / CA env name on the controller is the only path a trust-store change can break; the values stay unprinted
